title: Contrastive Perplexity for Controlled Generation: An Application in Detoxifying Large Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the detoxification rates (the reduction in generating toxic text) of Large Language Models when prompted with contexts targeting specific marginalized demographic groups, including religious groups such as Jewish and Muslim populations, using a Contrastive Perplexity (CP) fine-tuning framework.
findings: The study found that fine-tuning with the Contrastive Perplexity (CP) framework consistently reduced toxicity towards marginalized demographics, including religious groups. Specifically, when tested with Mistral-7b, the average toxicity rate dropped from 0.225 to 0.044 for the Jewish demographic, and from 0.391 to 0.053 for the Muslim demographic.
